 The Honourable Smt. Justice K. Sujana

sentences.text: Seeking the Court to enlarge the petitioner who is arrayed as accused in Crime No.83 of 2024 of Jagadgirigutta Police Station, Cyberabad Commissionerate, on bail, the present Criminal Petition is filed.

2. The brief facts of the case are that a 13-year-old girl named Laxmibai, a student at Ashoka Mentori Chanikya High School, went missing on 20.01.2024, from her home in H.No.4-53-163/1,
Ring Basthi, Jagadgirigutta.
Her father, Neethu Singh, reported the incident to the Police at 6:30 p.m. that same day, stating that Laxmibai had left home without any prior notice.
Thereafter, the police are investigating the matter, with suspicion falling on Sunil Rio Ringh Basthi, who has been in contact with the family and is known to them.

3. Heard Sri M. Ram Gopal Rao, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner as well as Sri Syed Yasar Mamoon, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of SKS,J respondent No.1-State and Sri S. Goutham, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is currently in judicial custody since 26.01.2024, at District Jail, Kandi, Sangareddy District, seeks regular bail.
The petitioner was granted bail on 19.03.2024, but it was later cancelled on 05.08.2024, with a directive to surrender by 19.08.2024.
However, the accused was rearrested on 31.08.2024, and has remained in custody since.

He further submitted that the allegations leveled against the petitioner are false, baseless, and the petitioner is an innocent person, falsely implicated by the complainant.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner and the families of the victim girl hail from the same village in Rajasthan and had intended to marry, but a dispute arose when the father of the accused disagreed with the victim's family and that the petitioner is a private employee and sole breadwinner, faces hardship and irreparable loss if detention continues.
As all the witnesses examined and except the charge sheet is pending, the petitioner promises to abide by any conditions, cooperate with the investigation, and SKS,J attend Court hearings.

The petitioner is willing to furnish reliable sureties and undertake to cooperate with the investigation agency, and therefore, prays for grant of regular bail.
6.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that the bail application of the petitioner should be opposed due to the heinous nature of the crimes committed against the Pichonia Sunil Goud vs The State Of Telangana, on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167106904/

sentences.text: 13-year-old daughter of respondent No.2.

The accused abducted, raped, and stole from the minor,
despite reports to the Police, which were initially ignored.

He further submitted that the police only conducted a medical examination after approaching the office of the Police Commissioner, and crucial evidence remains uninvestigated and that the accused has a history of predatory behavior,
manipulating and exploiting minors, and is facing similar charges in Rajasthan.
He contended that his previous conduct demonstrates a real and substantial danger of absconding or fleeing if released on bail.

Furthermore, the investigation is still in progress, and the release of the accused would obstruct further investigation, pose a threat to the family of respondent SKS,J No.2 and witnesses,
and embolden him to tamper with evidence and intimidate witnesses.

7. In support of his submissions, learned counsel for respondent No.2 relied upon the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bhagwan Singh v. Dilip Kumar 1 , has emphasized the gravity of rape and POCSO offences, and the bail applications of the accused have been consistently rejected due to the serious nature of the accusations against him.
Therefore, he prayed the Court to dismiss the criminal petition.
8. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the investigation is completed and charge sheet is also filed.
At this stage, granting of bail to the petitioner does not arise and if the petitioner is released on bail, he will not co
-operate with the trial.
Therefore, he prayed the Court to dismiss the criminal petition.

9. Considering the submissions presented by both the learned counsel and a thorough examination of the record, this Court observes that the Crime was registered on 20.01.2024, and the petitioner was subsequently released on 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1059 SKS,J bail, only to be rearrested on 31.08.2024.

A review of the record reveals that the petitioner intimidated the 13-year-old victim,
causing her to withhold disclosure of the incident.

However, upon the incarceration of the petitioner, the victim felt compelled to reveal the events of 20.01.2024, wherein she clandestinely exited her residence while her mother slept, contacted the petitioner via phone, and subsequently met him at the Secunderabad metro station.
The petitioner then accompanied the victim to Warangal, where they shared a hotel room, and the petitioner allegedly engaged in non- consensual sexual activity with the victim.

The following day, the petitioner and the victim traveled to Nagpur and later to Orai, Uttar Pradesh, where the petitioner again allegedly subjected the victim to physical exploitation at his friend's residence.

10. In light of these egregious allegations, coupled with the petitioner's reported intimidation of the victim, this Court is disinclined to grant bail to the petitioner, particularly in consideration of the tender age of the victim and the severity of the offences alleged, which include Sections 366 and 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code, as well as Sections 5(1) read with 6 SKS,J of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court does not find any merit in the criminal petition to grant pre-arrest bail to the petitioner and the same is liable to be dismissed.
11. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is dismissed.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
